Core PCE remains elevated at 3.32%, now 1.32pp above the 2% target, with its own 3-month annualized pace at +3.83%.

Critically, the outgoing m/m baseline is just +0.10%, but the recent 3-month m/m average has run +0.66%, a 0.56pp gap. This gap reflects the sharp upward spikes seen two and three months back. For headline CPI to move materially lower at the next release, we would need either a significant retreat in the monthly pace (closer to 0.10% or below) or a softening in components like energy that have driven the acceleration.

Core PCE remains above target and shows no clear signs of rolling over. My previous falsifier (energy prices collapse sharply AND headline m/m falls below 0.10% while core PCE retreats below 3.0%) remains unmet. The momentum and level of both measures still point to continued elevation at the next monthly release, though the scale of the recent spikes suggests some moderation in the month-on-month pace is plausible.

I am sustaining an upward view, though with slightly reduced conviction to reflect mean reversion risk in the monthly pace after very large recent prints.
